name: Agency delivery lab
description: Follow a project from discovery to handover. Product design (business analysts and requirements engineers) and technical design run in parallel into a Ready to build backlog that developers pull from; shared developers and QA create visible queues. Each step declares what earlier steps must deliver. Two project groups exercise both acceptance and rework. All values are synthetic.

steps.name: Project intake
steps.description: An approved project brief enters the agency delivery process.

steps.name: Discovery
steps.description: A product owner clarifies the problem, users and success measures.

steps.name: Plan together
steps.description: Product design and technical design run in parallel. Both are needed before work enters the backlog.

steps.name: Product design
steps.description: Business analysts and requirements engineers turn the framed problem into prioritised requirements and acceptance examples.

steps.name: Technical design
steps.description: An engineer defines integration seams and the implementation approach.

steps.name: Ready to build
steps.description: Designed projects wait in a bounded backlog, ordered by priority. Developers pull the next item when they have capacity.

steps.name: Implementation
steps.description: A developer implements the agreed feature. Shared capacity may create a queue.

steps.name: Quality review
steps.description: QA checks the feature against its acceptance examples.

steps.name: Accepted?
steps.description: Cases marked needsRework take one rework loop; other cases proceed to handover.

steps.name: Resolve findings
steps.description: Correct the findings and clear needsRework before QA checks the project again.

steps.name: Client handover
steps.description: The product owner hands over the accepted increment and supporting documentation.

steps.name: Delivered
steps.description: The project case is complete. Its cycle time contributes to the run metrics.
